title: U.S. House, District 17
counties: Lee (part, incl. more of Fort Myers)
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 17th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: Roster from WSLR (Matt Montavon wins Congressional District 17 primary; Steube unopposed in GOP primary) and Ballotpedia. No NPA or write-in candidate was identified in snippets; absence unconfirmed. Sources: https://wslr.org/matt-montavon-wins-congressional-district-17-primary/ ; https://ballotpedia.org/Florida's_17th_Congressional_District_election,_2026 ; district changes per WUSF map breakdown. Florida adopted a new congressional map (passed Apr 29, 2026, signed May 4, 2026) that reworked 21 of 28 districts; county descriptions here reflect post-redistricting reporting where found (https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-05-06/breakdown-changes-for-florida-new-congressional-map).

candidates.name: Greg Steube
candidates.photo_source: congress.gov member portrait (bioguide ID from memory, unverified)
candidates.background: Greg Steube has represented Florida's 17th District since January 2019 and previously served in the Florida House and Senate; he sits on the House Ways and Means Committee. He was unopposed in the Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary. Under the 2026 map the district gives up inland eastern Sarasota County and takes in more of Fort Myers in Lee County.

taxes.summary: Steube voted for H.R. 1 (the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) on final passage in July 2025. The law made the 2017 individual tax-rate cuts permanent and added new deductions while reducing projected federal spending on Medicaid and SNAP.

candidates.name: Matthew Montavon
candidates.occupation: Retired; former United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization official (27 years); former local-government planner; Peace Corps volunteer
candidates.background: Matthew (Matt) Montavon grew up in Indiana, served two years in the Peace Corps and spent 27 years with the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization in Rome, where he helped run a department with a $50 million budget; he also worked in local-government planning. Now retired in suburban Sarasota, he has been active in the local Democratic Party and co-founded the Suncoast Immigration Justice Coalition. He won the Aug. 18, 2026 Democratic primary with nearly 55% of the vote, defeating Allen Spence by roughly 5,000 votes, and faces incumbent Greg Steube in November.
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug 18, 2026 Democratic primary with ~55% over Allen Spence (WSLR)
